report.summary: Detector fired on gross BUY size vs depth and a SELL fill of 80 followed by a BUY cancel. The tape shows a pegged execution algo re-pricing two parent orders (P-T-X1105-04-B and -S). The 2211-lot children are refreshed on both sides, one after the other. Cancels are symmetric (0.9987). Orders sit at the touch and are 0.87x depth, so none is large. The 80 SELL fill was on the algo's own sell child. The price moved -0.5 ticks with no reversion. Feature (a) and feature (b) are both absent.

evidence.fact: All orders are PEGGED children of parents P-T-X1105-04-B and P-T-X1105-04-S. Each 2211-lot child is cancelled and replaced within milliseconds, alternating BUY and SELL, with the pegged price following best bid/ask changes (e.g. ask 10002 to 10001).
The only execution is a PARTIAL_FILL of 80 on SELL order O-00024082 at 10001 at 13:52:47.480. The BUY order was cancelled at 13:52:50.704 and replaced at once by O-00024088 of 2211.

response.final_text:
**Proposed disposition:** CLOSE_FP, confidence 0.85. It is recorded as a proposal, awaiting a human decision (case C-A-261105-0004).

**Three facts that drove it:**
1. Every order is a PEGGED child of parent P-T-X1105-04-B or P-T-X1105-04-S. The 2211-lot children are refreshed alternately on both sides, and cancel_symmetry is 0.9987. This points to algorithmic re-pricing.
2. The orders are at the touch (0 ticks) and peak at 0.87x depth, so no single order is large. The only execution is an 80-lot partial fill on the algo's own SELL child. Price moved -0.5 ticks with no reversion, so I found no benefit from an opposite-side execution.
3. There were no public events, no risk events and no repetition. The trader has no prior alerts.

The desk notes for ALGO-EXEC concern a different trader, so I used them only as context. Today's tape supports the same explanation independently.

**What would change my mind:** a pegged child sitting one-sided or away from the touch, or a favourable price move that reverts after the BUY cancel. The order-to-trade ratio of 58 against a typical 25 is noted, but the quote-refresh pattern explains it.
